deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is an administrative slip on blue paper, almost certainly a library loan request (Göttingen University Library). It reads: 'Riess. Reibungselectricität. Bd. 1. Berlin. 1853 / Bd. 2. Berlin 1853.' and is signed 'B. Riemann' with an address in parentheses. The requested work is Peter Theophil Riess, 'Die Lehre von der Reibungselektricität', 2 volumes, Berlin (Hirschwald) 1853, the standard comprehensive treatise of the time on electrostatics. A different, later hand has added a shelf or locator mark in pink/red ink at the left ('Fach 58' or 'Fasc. 58'; my reading, uncertain). A small '50' at the right edge is the archival folio number. A large pencil loop with a diagonal stroke runs across the middle. It looks like a cancellation mark, for example made when the book was returned or the request was processed. It is not a diagram. Context: the previous folio is Riemann's 1860 announcement of a lecture course on the mathematical theory of gravity, electricity and magnetism. Riemann also published work in 1854–55 on the distribution of electricity in ponderable bodies (residual charge of the Leyden jar, Nobili rings), where Riess's experimental results were a central reference. So the slip documents his reading in experimental electrostatics, either for that research or for the lectures. It cannot be dated precisely from the page. It is not before 1853, the publication year.

results.what: Library request for P. T. Riess, Die Lehre von der Reibungselektricität, vols. 1–2 (Berlin 1853)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a book-loan slip with no mathematical content. Riemann's use of Riess's standard electrostatics treatise is entirely expected, given his published 1854–55 work on electrical distribution and residual charge and his lectures on electricity.
transcription_corrections: The parenthetical address under the signature is uncertain. It reads something like '(Weststr.)'/'(Wegstr.)'; 'Weißstr.' is doubtful and it may be a Göttingen street name such as Weender Str. It should be marked illegible or uncertain.
The pink/red marginal note at left is better read as a shelf/locator mark ('Fach 58' or 'Fasc. 58'), in a different hand and ink from Riemann's.
The '50' at the right edge is the archival folio number, not part of Riemann's text.
The large pencil loop and diagonal stroke are not transcribed. They are probably a cancellation/processing mark, not a figure.
Full title of the cited book: 'Die Lehre von der Reibungselektricität' (Riess, Berlin 1853, 2 Bde.).
